## The study

This study compares mortality and graft outcomes after simultaneous liver–kidney (SLK) transplantation between recipients with and without HIV, using Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) data. [Study design and methods](study_methods.qmd) explains how.

The analysis is preliminary and not for citation. Early results were presented as a poster at the NY-NJ Center for AIDS Research 2026 regional conference, shown on the [home page](../index.qmd); the manuscript is in preparation.

-   **Hannah Rosenthal**
-   **Christina Tsai**
-   **Jonathan Mamber Czeresnia**

Scientific decisions are made by Vagish Hemmige. Open decisions are marked in the analysis plan and listed in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-SLK-outcomes/issues).

## This repository

`R/main.R` runs the scripts in order: importing the transplant files, building the SLK cohort, adding donor and candidate data, matching, and producing tables and figures. The SRTR standard analysis files are loaded through the [sRtr](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr) package. SRTR data are restricted under a data use agreement, so they are not in the repository; the code runs only where an authorized person has access to them.

Contributions follow the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](agents.qmd); known issues and open decisions are tracked in [Issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-SLK-outcomes/issues). To comment on any page, highlight the text and use the Comment button; comments are filed as GitHub issues.

## How this website was created

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from the analysis scripts themselves. Each code page shows its script from `R/` with an explanation; until a script is divided into labelled sections, its page shows the script whole. The site never runs the analysis, so it is built without the restricted SRTR data. A GitHub Actions workflow renders and publishes it whenever `master` changes.

The repository is maintained with the [R Analysis Workflow](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/r-analysis-workflow) plugin for AI coding assistants, written by Vagish Hemmige. The plugin provides the repository layout, the conventions for the analysis plan and `AGENTS.md`, and the format of these pages. AI assistants may help draft and review code and documentation under the rules in `AGENTS.md`: they work only with code, documentation and synthetic data, never with SRTR data, every change reaches `master` through a pull request a person reviews and merges, and every scientific decision is made by the investigator and recorded in a GitHub issue.

Four documents describe the project. In short: the plan is the scientific intent, the architecture is the workflow as implemented, and `AGENTS.md` holds the rules for working together.

-   [**Analysis plan**](analysis-plan.qmd): *what the analysis is meant to do, and why.* The question, the population, the exposure, matching, the outcomes, the statistical methods, and the open decisions. Code implements it and does not redefine it.
-   [**Architecture**](architecture.qmd): *how the code does it.* The scripts, the order they run in, what each needs and produces, and how data flow between them.
-   [**AGENTS.md**](agents.qmd): *how people and AI assistants work on the project.* Rules for restricted data, coding, checks, proposing changes and getting a person's approval.
-   [**Repository blueprint**](repository-blueprint.qmd): *the layout every project of this kind starts from*, which the architecture document then describes as built.

## Pages

-   [**Methodological background**](methodological_background.qmd): the SRTR files, linking liver and kidney records, matching and survival analysis, in general terms (being written).
-   [**Study design and methods**](study_methods.qmd): what this study chose, linked to the plan and its open decisions (being written).
-   [**Setup**](setup.qmd): packages and shared constants.
-   [**Functions**](functions.qmd): helper functions, including harmonizing liver and kidney records.
-   [**Tables**](tables.qmd) and [**Figures**](figures.qmd): building and exporting the outputs.
